Hi Tom / team,

Thanks again for taking time today — helpful call. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we all have the same checklist:  

Recap:  
- Scope: fully air-gapped, on-prem deployment of Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem package) for inference and logging to a customer-controlled SIEM.
- Security controls: HSM for key storage, no egress allowed from inference cluster, onsite-only updates via our appliance image + signed packages.
- Workload: bursty inference for fraud-detection models (peaks ~600 qps, typical 120 qps), avg seq length ~256 tokens, expected concurrency ~80.

Open items we need to validate:  
1) Hardware baseline: Do you prefer headroom (H100-class) or cost-optimal A100 nodes? We typically recommend H100 for futureproofing on large context models; sketch below.
2) Procurement timeline: target provisioning date for onsite hardware / rack space.
3) Offline ops: who will own day-to-day offline upgrades/patching? We provide a runbook + signed artifacts for air-gapped upgrade flows but need the local ops owner and maintenance windows.
4) Power/cooling & network: confirm PDU capacity, cross-connect timing, and whether maintenance VLANs are available for the appliance.

Attachments: redwood_onprem_requirements_v2.pdf (deployment checklist) and initial_mop_checklist.xlsx (MOP for offline upgrades).

Suggested next steps:  
- Tom: please fill the checklist and attach your network diagram.
- We (Dev + me): will propose two hardware bundles (cost-optimal A100 bundle + performance H100 bundle) and propose an offline upgrade cadence and rollback plan.
- Follow-up call next week to finalize procurement/PO timing.

If you can send the network diagram and confirm who owns onsite upgrades by EOD Tuesday, we’ll turn around hardware specs + SOW draft.

Thanks,

Hi Tom / Sarah — great, thanks for the details and the diagram — very helpful. A few technical notes based on the workload you shared:  

Hardware recommendation (short):  
- Performance (recommended, futureproof): 4x NVIDIA H100 SXM nodes (each node dual-GPU equivalent) with 1.6TB NVMe per node for model+KV cache, roughly 24TB total working set; expected sustained throughput for 600 qps peaks with room for model upgrades.
- Cost-optimal: 6x A100 80GB cards across 3 nodes with similar NVMe; lower upfront cost but less headroom for large-context models.

Upgrade strategy for air-gapped:  
- Rolling upgrades: supported but require a maintenance window and staged image uploads via signed USB/air-gapped transfer package. We provide checksums and an automated verifier to run pre- and post-upgrade.
- Standby cluster: recommended if you require zero-downtime during major model swaps; otherwise 4-6 hour rolling maintenance windows are typical and acceptable for most detection workloads.

Attachment: hw_specs_A100_vs_H100.pdf with lab estimates and cost delta.

Action items I’ll take: produce a formal hardware BOM for both bundles and a runbook for the offline upgrade flow (signed artifacts + verifier). Can you confirm whether Sarah’s team prefers a standby cluster or rolling maintenance? Also please confirm rack PDU connector types (we saw 60A but need exact connector).

Thanks,
